cases.sentence: Пьер подошел к костру, поел жареного ___, лег спиной к огню и тотчас же заснул.
cases.explain: «лошадиного мяса» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The stores, the prisoners, and the marshal’s baggage train stopped at the village of Shámshevo. The men crowded together round the campfires. Pierre went up to the fire, ate some roast horseflesh, lay down with his back to the fire, and immediately fell asleep. He again slept as he had done at Mozháysk after the battle of Borodinó.

cases.sentence: У костра, присев на корточках, сидел француз, только что оттолкнувший ___, и жарил надетое на шомпол мясо.
cases.explain: «русского солдата» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: He lifted himself and sat up. A Frenchman who had just pushed a Russian soldier away was squatting by the fire, engaged in roasting a piece of meat stuck on a ramrod. His sleeves were rolled up and his sinewy, hairy, red hands with their short fingers deftly turned the ramrod. His brown morose face with frowning brows was clearly visible by the glow of the charcoal.

cases.sentence: Жилистые, засученные, обросшие волосами, ___, с короткими пальцами ловко поворачивали шомпол.
cases.explain: «красные руки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: He lifted himself and sat up. A Frenchman who had just pushed a Russian soldier away was squatting by the fire, engaged in roasting a piece of meat stuck on a ramrod. His sleeves were rolled up and his sinewy, hairy, red hands with their short fingers deftly turned the ramrod. His brown morose face with frowning brows was clearly visible by the glow of the charcoal.

cases.sentence: — прокричал один из них и через минуту толпа ___ окружила Пьера.
cases.explain: «русских лиц» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “The Cossacks!” one of them shouted, and a moment later a crowd of Russians surrounded Pierre.

cases.sentence: — плача кричали ___, обнимая казаков и гусар.
cases.explain: «старые солдаты» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Brothers! Dear fellows! Darlings!” old soldiers exclaimed, weeping, as they embraced Cossacks and hussars. The hussars and Cossacks crowded round the prisoners; one offered them clothes, another boots, and a third bread. Pierre sobbed as he sat among them and could not utter a word. He hugged the first soldier who approached him, and kissed him, weeping.

cases.sentence: — Filez, filez,[993] Проходи, проходи, — приговаривал Долохов, выучившись этому выражению у французов и, встречаясь глазами с проходившими пленными, взгляд его вспыхивал ___.
cases.explain: «жестоким блеском» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Filez, filez!”127 Dólokhov kept saying, having adopted this expression from the French, and when his eyes met those of the prisoners they flashed with a cruel light.

cases.sentence: Денисов с ___, сняв папаху, шел позади казаков, несших к вырытой в саду яме тело Пети Ростова.
cases.explain: «мрачным лицом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Denísov, bareheaded and with a gloomy face, walked behind some Cossacks who were carrying the body of Pétya Rostóv to a hole that had been dug in the garden.
